subject: general
question: Which of the following is a pivotal joint in the human body?

options.text: Joint where our neck joins the head
Joint between the upper jaw and the rest of the head

solution:
The correct answer is Joint where our neck joins the head.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A joint is the part of the body where two or more bones meet in order to allow movement.
 
• In general, the more the range of movement, the higher the risk of injury because the strength of the joint is reduced due to more range of movement.
 
• 
 
There are a total of three broad classes of joints which are- 

 

 
• 
 
Immovable Joints – in which the two or more bones are in close contact, but no movement can occur – for example, the bones of the skull.

 
 
• 
 
Slightly movable – in this joint two or more bones are held together so tightly that only limited movement is permitted – for example, the vertebrae of the spine

 
 
• 
 
Freely movable – most joints of the human body are of this type. The purpose of this joint to allow movement of the bones.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The six types of a freely movable joint include

 
• Ball and Socket- example- such as the hip joint or shoulder joint.
 
• Saddle- example- joint at the base of the thumb.
 
• Hinge- example- the knee and elbow joints.
 
• Condyloid- for example- the jaw or finger joints.
 
• Pivot- example- the joint between the first and second vertebrae in the neck.
 
• Gliding/Plane- example- wrist joints.
